idiom_name: [Struct] via GRDB FetchableRecord.fetchAll / SQLite.swift row mapping
implementation_notes: Swift's record set is an array of Decodable structs: GRDB fetches rows into any type conforming to FetchableRecord (struct OrderRow: FetchableRecord, Decodable { ... } then try OrderRow.fetchAll(db, sql: "SELECT ...")), and SQLite.swift maps each row of a prepared statement the same way; GRDB also exposes Row itself - values addressable by index or column name - for genuinely dynamic queries, which is the closest library equivalent of a classic record set. What replaces the classic structure is the struct plus the array, with the column contract encoded in the decoding/CodingKeys. Apple's Core Data goes the other way (context-bound NSManagedObject instances, not a detached tabular value) and should be mapped to structs before leaving the persistence layer.
pitfalls: A GRDB Row is backed by the SQLite statement: decode inside the fetch request - escaping a Row reference out of the statement is undefined behaviour, so fetchAll of a struct is the safe materialised form.
Column-name-to-property matching happens in decoding: a renamed or missing column throws at fetch time - explicit CodingKeys decouples the struct from SQL aliases.
Core Data results are context-bound and faulting; passing them between contexts/threads raises concurrency errors - map to structs at the boundary.
